name: Cro-Mags
label: Victory
lede: Lower East Side kids, a Hare Krishna singer and a bassist who'd been in a punk band since he was eleven made the New York hardcore record every other band gets measured against. Then they spent forty years in court, and once backstage with a knife, over who owns the name.

eras.title: From a goof band to Cro-Mags
eras.text: Harley Flanagan dates the band to 1980, John Joseph to 1981, and the lineup changed too fast to settle it. The cast: Lower East Side kids, a Bad Brains roadie who found Krishna, and a drummer turned bassist who'd been playing in a punk band since he was eleven.

years.h: The first Cro-Mags are a joke band called Disco Smoothy
years.p: By Harley Flanagan's account, they debuted at the Peppermint Lounge with Dave Stein on guitar, Dave Hahn on drums and John Berry singing.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the Disco Smoothy set opened for [[The Stimulators|498b08a4-b2ec-48f9-a201-1ea856a548b4]], the band of Flanagan's aunt, Denise Mercedes. Flanagan was 11 when he started drumming for them, and he'd dropped out of school in seventh grade. At nine he'd published a book of poems and drawings with a foreword by Allen Ginsberg.

The founding date is its own feud. Flanagan's 2016 memoir Hard-Core: Life of My Own says 1980; Joseph's 2007 book The Evolution of a Cro-Magnon says 1981. The band also played as Mode of Ignorance before settling on Cro-Mags.

years.big: I was way too serious about my shit
years.h: Bad Brains roadie John Joseph sings, but skips the Smoothy gig
years.p: That's how Joseph says he answered Flanagan's offer to play the Peppermint Lounge as 'The Disco Smoothies'. He'd come out of foster homes, the streets and a year in the Navy, and roadying for [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] had led him to yoga, meditation and plant-based eating.
years.xp:
Joseph's 2007 book places it in the late summer of 1981: he was hanging out with Flanagan again when the first lineup came together, with Flanagan on bass, Hahn on drums, Stein on guitar and Joseph on vocals. Flanagan wanted the Peppermint Lounge show 'as a goof', he writes.

Joseph joined the Navy in 1980 and went AWOL after a year. In 1982 he became a Hare Krishna devotee, and later ran a homeless food program in Tompkins Square Park. Bad Brains singer H.R. told him he had too much energy to be a drummer and should sing.

years.h: Todd Youth, sneaking into the city since sixth grade, takes the bass
years.p: Harley Flanagan moves to drums, and starts [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]] with Jimmy Dreschler the same year. H.R. of [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] gave Youth his nickname for those trips into the city.

years.big: Harley would see some kid with a shaved head and think 'This kid is hard... let's bring him into the band.'
years.h: Eric Casanova sings, Roger Miret plays bass, Mackie Jayson drums
years.p: That's guitarist Parris Mayhew on how Flanagan recruited. In 1983 the results were Casanova on vocals, future [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] singer Miret on bass for a year, and Jayson on drums.
years.xp:
Mayhew, in the 2014 book NYHC: New York Hardcore 1980-1990, goes on: 'Then I would end up tolerating some horrible, talentless person for however long it took Harley to realise that the guy had no talent.'

Casanova didn't last. Flanagan's memoir says he was about 15 when 'he got his girlfriend pregnant and left to try and do the right thing.' Joseph took the vocals in 1984.

years.h: Joseph is back at the mic, and Casanova is gone
years.p: Harley Flanagan returns to bass, setting up the lineup that will make The Age of Quarrel. Fan video from CBGB on June 15, 1985, catches the band in that period.

eras.title: The record, then the exit
eras.text: One album on Profile Records bent New York hardcore toward metal and toward Krishna at the same time. Parris Mayhew and Flanagan wrote most of it, Joseph sang it, and a year later he was out.

years.cap: The Age of Quarrel, Profile Records, 1986
years.src: Wikipedia: The Age of Quarrel · Wikipedia: Cro-Mags
years.h: The Age of Quarrel lands on Profile Records
years.p: Recorded at Eastside Studios in New York with producer Chris Williamson and engineer Steve Remote. The title translates Kali Yuga, the Hindu age of spiritual decline.
years.xp:
Several songs grew out of a four-track demo Flanagan recorded alone in 1982 while on the West Coast, per Wikipedia. Mayhew has said Rush directly inspired several of the riffs.

AllMusic gives it 4.5 stars. Hit Parader ranked it the fourth greatest hardcore album in 2007; Revolver put it 22nd among the greatest punk albums in 2018, and its readers voted it the greatest NYHC album in 2024. [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s Jamey Jasta calls it one of the most crucial albums in hardcore history.

yt: Live at The Ritz, New York, April 5, 1986
years.h: MTV puts Cro-Mags slam dancing on Headbangers Ball
years.p: Mayhew directed the We Gotta Know clip, which also ran on 120 Minutes. Wikipedia calls it one of the first MTV videos to show slam dancing and crowd surfing. Below, the band live at the Ritz that April.
years.xp: [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] singer Karl Buechner has said the We Gotta Know video was the spark that got him into hardcore. In a 1996 interview he called the album 'still the greatest hardcore album of all time'.

years.h: Joseph is expelled, and Flanagan takes the vocals too
years.p: Wikipedia dates the expulsion to 1987. Harley Flanagan keeps playing bass and sings, and John Joseph won't return for four years.

eras.title: Metal years, and a mic that keeps moving
eras.text: With Flanagan on vocals, the band went metal and spent two months on the road with the German thrash band Destruction. Joseph returned in 1991 for two Century Media albums, and who wrote what became the next argument.

years.h: Best Wishes gets cut in a couple of days, and the drummer leaves mid-session
years.p: At Normandy Sound in Warren, Rhode Island, Flanagan sings for the first time on a Cro-Mags album. Drummer Pete Hines walks out, scared of a supposed local ghost.
years.xp:
Guitarist Doug Holland was battling heroin addiction and on methadone during the sessions, and Mayhew ended up playing his parts on four of the eight songs. Mayhew says Joseph left because 'he was hiding, stalling and making excuses for his inability to find a melody.'

The songs run about four minutes each against under two on the debut, with longer structures and guitar solos. AllMusic says the album 'rocks ferociously while expressing a very Hindu viewpoint'. Kerrang! put it at No. 36 on its 2019 list of the 50 best albums of 1989, calling it 'a perfect example of crossover done correctly'.

years.h: Destruction opens the Down But Not Out tour
years.p: From April 14 to June 24, Cro-Mags play Best Wishes with the German thrash band as support.

years.h: Joseph returns, and Mayhew walks
years.p: John Joseph is back as singer, and co-founder Parris Mayhew leaves, not to return until 1999. Below, the band live at CBGB on May 8, 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alpha Omega (Cro-Mags album) · Wikipedia: John Joseph (singer)
years.h: Alpha Omega lands on Century Media, and so does the argument over who wrote it
years.p: Mayhew says he wrote most of the songs with Rob Buckley, though neither plays on the record. Flanagan disputes that.
years.xp:
The album was recorded in 1991 at Normandy Sound in Warren, Rhode Island, and produced by Tom Soares. Joseph sang; Holland played lead guitar, Gabby Abularach rhythm and Dave DiCenso drums. Mayhew and Buckley aren't on it.

AllMusic's Vincent Jeffries wrote that it 'delivers a steady stream of straightforward metal' but 'falls short of its creators' best work'. Joseph's own Wikipedia entry credits him with the lyrics here, as on The Age of Quarrel and Near Death Experience.

years.h: Near Death Experience is the last record with Joseph and Doug Holland
years.p: Harley Flanagan produces it. The band then goes on hiatus, and the next album, Revenge, is seven years away.
years.xp: Recorded in 1993 at Normandy Sound and Unique Studios in New York for Century Media, with Gabby Abularach on rhythm guitar and Dave di Censo on drums. The lyrics touch on environmentalism, anti-abortion positions and spirituality. AllMusic rated it 2.5 stars.

eras.title: Revenge, then too many Cro-Mags
eras.text: Flanagan and Mayhew teamed up with Rocky George for one album, then fell out for good. By then rival versions of the band were touring as Cro-Mag Jam, Street Justice and Cholo-Mags.

years.h: Flanagan and Mayhew reunite for Revenge
years.p: The first Cro-Mags album in seven years has Harley Flanagan singing and Rocky George on lead guitar.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, many fans heard it as a return to the band's early hardcore roots.

years.h: After the Revenge tour, Mayhew and Flanagan are done
years.p: The tour ends in lasting resentment between them. Through the 1990s and 2000s, Flanagan and Joseph sometimes run separate Cro-Mags at the same time.
years.xp:
Those parallel versions billed themselves as Cro-Mag Jam, Street Justice, Age of Quarrel, FVK (Fearless Vampire Killers) or Cholo-Mags, each with a different lineup.

Flanagan asked Joseph to rejoin in 2001, and the reunion ended in 2002. By 2003 the band had stopped.

eras.title: Two Cro-Mags, one knife
eras.text: Joseph and Mackie Jayson put a Cro-Mags back on stage without Flanagan. The feud turned physical at Webster Hall in 2012, legal in 2018, and ended with one man owning the name.

years.h: Joseph and Mackie Jayson restart Cro-Mags without Flanagan
years.p: Craig Setari of [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] plays bass and A.J. Novello of [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]] plays guitar.

years.h: Harley Flanagan is arrested after a backstage fight at Webster Hall
years.p: At a show by Joseph's Cro-Mags, Flanagan was arrested for allegedly stabbing two band members and biting one. He said they attacked him in the dressing room and he drew a knife in self-defense.
years.xp: Flanagan was stabbed in the leg and needed 30 stitches. Prosecutors dropped the criminal charges in December 2012 for lack of cooperating witnesses, and a later civil suit was dismissed.

years.h: Joseph finishes his first Ironman, five weeks after Webster Hall
years.p: He'd run the Marine Corps Marathon in 2007; the singer's first triathlon was on August 11, 2012.

years.h: Dave Stein, the first Cro-Mags guitarist, dies
years.p: Stein played guitar in Harley Flanagan's earliest version of the band.

years.h: Flanagan's memoir Hard-Core: Life of My Own comes out on Feral House
years.p: A solo album titled Cro-Mags arrives alongside it. John Berry, singer in the earliest lineup, dies the same year.
years.xp: The book is where Flanagan dates the band to 1980. He also writes that he met Parris Mayhew around then through 'my crazy-ass Skinhead friend Paul Dordal'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Harley Flanagan · Wikipedia: John Joseph (singer)
years.h: Flanagan sues Joseph and Jayson over the Cro-Mags name
years.p: The federal trademark suit is filed in the Southern District of New York. Flanagan also has major back surgery for a spinal cord injury this year.
years.xp: The complaint names Joseph by his legal name, John McGowan, and Jayson as Maxwell Jayson.

years.h: Todd Youth dies at 47
years.p: After Cro-Mags he played in [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]], [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]], [[D Generation|75a14804-749e-4a5a-b445-4388596b760b]] and [[Danzig|8925a01a-8608-411d-a90b-f3a52d061208]], and in 2017 with John Joseph in Bloodclot.

years.h: Flanagan wins the Cro-Mags name, and Joseph's band becomes Cro-Mags JM
years.p: Harley Flanagan holds exclusive rights. Joseph and Jayson can keep playing under a limited license from August 2019, as Cro-Mags JM.

eras.title: Harley's Cro-Mags
eras.text: With the name settled, Flanagan rebuilt the band around himself and released its first new music in nineteen years. The next fight, over a single letter, ended in front of a federal judge too.

years.h: Nineteen years later, Don't Give In
years.p: Drag You Under and No One's Victim arrive with it, ahead of tour dates with the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]]. Flanagan sings and plays bass, with Rocky George on lead guitar.

years.h: Phil Campbell of [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]] plays on the From the Grave 7-inch
years.p: The three-song single, out December 6, also carries PTSD and Between Wars.

years.h: Lockdown, so Cro-Mags stream a free show from SIR Studios
years.p: A March 15 Webster Hall date with Body Count had been postponed. The band was one of the first to livestream a concert in the early weeks of COVID-19.

years.h: In the Beginning ends a 20-year wait for a Cro-Mags album
years.p: Harley Flanagan's lineup makes the band's sixth studio album, previewed by a free download of The Final Test on March 31.

years.h: A federal judge gives Flanagan the Cro-Mags name for good
years.p: Joseph's license to play as Cro-Mags JM is revoked after he billed his band as Cro-Mags JAM, and a federal court in New York grants Flanagan a permanent injunction. Joseph said in 2024 he'll never reunite with the classic lineup.
years.xp: The court found Joseph had violated the 2019 settlement by using JAM instead of JM.

years.h: Flanagan gets a documentary, then a hot sauce
years.p: Harley Flanagan: Wired for Chaos premieres in 2024. In December he launches a hot sauce called Age of Hot Sauce.

years.h: Pete Hines, the Best Wishes drummer, rejoins Cro-Mags
years.p: Hines last played with the band in 1989. The first East Coast tour with him in more than 35 years follows that month.

years.h: BLKIIBLK Records signs Cro-Mags
years.p: In June they release Wired for Chaos, their first new song in six years, and announce an album for 2027.

years.h: Forty years on, Flanagan re-cuts The Age of Quarrel
years.p: Scheduled for November 13 as The Age of Quarrel: 40 Years of Quarrel, previewed in August by a new World Peace. Flanagan said that month he's stepping back from regular touring.
